llm.summary: This skill is coherent, but it deserves review because it stores sensitive emotional and identity-like journal data in Notion and uses broad Notion/write/install mechanisms that need tight scoping.

dimensions.detail: Node, explicit Notion IDs, and Notion credentials are proportionate to the purpose, but NOTIONCTL_PATH can redirect execution to any existing local JavaScript file and the child process inherits the caller environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package itself has no third-party runtime dependencies, but the README instructs users to install notion-api-automation through unpinned npx/pnpm dlx clawhub@latest commands, making the effective installer mutable over time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill includes useful boundaries such as avoiding automatic USER.md promotion, honoring local-only requests, and limiting recall claims, but it also recommends heartbeat, daily journal, and ambient recall workflows that can persist conversation-derived emotional data without per-entry consent or retention controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifacts can create and patch Notion databases, write long-lived Notion pages containing memory/state/journal data, and write local ambient recall state and receipts; they do not install OS-level services, but scheduled use is recommended and externally configured.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the implemented Notion-backed memory, emotion/state, journal, and recall scripts, but the shared Notion bridge also exposes generic API, page, database, and schema mutation helpers beyond a narrowly scoped journaling interface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want an agent to store emotional, journal, and self-state material in Notion. Restrict the Notion integration to the specific parent page or databases, pin the dependency installer instead of using @latest, avoid NOTIONCTL_PATH unless the target file is trusted, and decide up front how cron, ambient recall, deletion, and retention should work.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The setup behavior is disclosed and purpose-aligned: setup_ltm.js creates or reuses the five Notion databases needed for memory, events, emotions, state, and journal data under a user-supplied parent page. It is not hidden tool poisoning, but it should be treated as an admin/setup workflow.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced scripts were present in the artifact and were inspected locally, so the partial-inspection concern is not supported after this review.
[RA1] unexpected: The cited text is an error hint telling the operator to update a dependency or set NOTIONCTL_PATH; I did not find code that modifies this skill's own SKILL.md, scripts, or configuration at runtime.
[SDI-1] expected: Creating, querying, and patching Notion resources is partly expected for this skill's storage model, but the helper surface is broader than the five configured databases and contributes to the Review verdict.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The generic httpJson passthrough is not necessary as a user-facing capability and can call arbitrary Notion API paths permitted by the configured token, so this overbroad escape hatch is accepted as a real concern.
[MP3] expected: Ambient recall staging and local state updates are core to the skill; the specific cited delete operation only removes an internal load-error field, not agent policy memory. The broader memory-reuse workflow remains sensitive and should be user-controlled.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The README is primarily Japanese, but the runtime SKILL.md does not instruct the agent to force Japanese responses or override the user's language preference.
[SSD-3] expected: External persistence of emotions, self-state, conversations, work summaries, future plans, and journals is the skill's disclosed purpose, but the sensitivity and long-term retention implications are material user-review concerns.
[RP1] unexpected: Installing the dependent Notion automation skill is expected, but using clawhub@latest through package runners is not necessary and adds mutable supply-chain risk.
[T08] unexpected: The SARIF unpinned package-runner finding is supported by README install commands that execute clawhub@latest rather than a pinned, reviewed version.
[T07] unexpected: The NOTIONCTL_PATH override is operationally understandable, but it executes the selected file with Node after only an existence check, with inherited environment credentials.
[T09] expected: The multi-step Notion event/emotion/state writes are expected for the schema, but they are non-transactional and can leave partial or duplicate continuity records if a later request fails.
